title: DOGE AI Surveillance Program Monitors Federal Employees for Anti-Trump Sentiment
description_short: DOGE AI Surveillance Program Monitors Federal Employees for Anti-Trump Sentiment
description_medium: Reuters reported in April 2025 that DOGE used AI to monitor communications at at least one federal agency for language hostile to Donald Trump or Elon Musk. The report also described DOGE personnel using Signal and raised questions about secrecy. It did not identify every agency, explain the tool’s scope or report specific discipline resulting from the monitoring.
description_long: Reuters reported in April 2025 that federal employees at at least one agency were told DOGE was using artificial-intelligence tools to monitor internal communications for language hostile to Donald Trump or Elon Musk. The supplied source note says the reporting also described DOGE personnel using Signal for their own communications and raised concerns about secrecy. The reported system concerned employees’ communications and political sentiment inside the federal workforce, rather than a publicly described performance or fraud audit. Such monitoring raises questions about privacy, oversight and the use of government technology to assess workers’ views, particularly when the criteria include hostility toward the president or his agenda. The available account does not identify all affected agencies, explain which messages the system could access, say whether the tool was deployed government-wide, or document discipline or other consequences for employees. Reuters’ linked page returned HTTP 401 during retrieval, so the scope cannot be checked directly here. The record can describe the reported monitoring at at least one agency but should not portray it as a fully documented government-wide political intelligence program without additional evidence.
subcategory: Reported AI monitoring of federal employee communications

title: Peter Navarro Indicted for Contempt of Congress Over Jan. 6 Subpoena
description_short: Peter Navarro Indicted for Contempt of Congress Over Jan. 6 Subpoena
description_medium: Former Trump trade adviser Peter Navarro was indicted in June 2022 on two contempt-of-Congress counts after refusing a January 6 committee subpoena; the supplied account says he asserted executive privilege, was later convicted and received a four-month sentence. The linked New York Times article is about Trump’s 2023 indictment, not Navarro’s case, so the facts need a case-specific source.
description_long: Peter Navarro, a former trade adviser to Donald Trump, was indicted on June 3, 2022, on two counts of contempt of Congress after refusing to comply with a subpoena from the House committee investigating January 6. The supplied account says Navarro claimed executive privilege on Trump’s behalf, was arrested at a Nashville airport and later complained that he had been placed in leg irons. It also says he was convicted in September 2023 and sentenced to four months in prison. Navarro had publicly discussed the “Green Bay Sweep,” a plan to delay certification of the 2020 election, in his own book. These details place the subpoena dispute in the committee’s examination of efforts to challenge the election result and explain why his refusal became a high-profile contempt prosecution. The linked New York Times URL, however, covers Trump’s separate August 2023 indictment and does not substantiate Navarro’s indictment, arrest or conviction. The event description reflects the supplied facts, but a contemporaneous Navarro case source is needed before the entry can be marked complete.
organization_tags: U.S. House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack
